ai.description: The King Cobra is the world’s longest venomous snake, reaching 5.8 meters. It is olive, tan, or black with pale chevron bands and features a distinctive hood with a chevron marking on the nape.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of a King Cobra is the pair of large, distinct occipital scales located on the back of the head, which are absent in other cobras.
ai.habitat: The King Cobra inhabits dense upland forests, bamboo thickets, and mangroves across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The King Cobra is primarily diurnal, actively hunting other snakes by tracking their scent trails across the forest floor using its highly sensitive forked tongue.
ai.reproductionNotes: King Cobras are oviparous, breeding from January to April. Females construct unique leaf-litter nests, laying clutches of 20–50 eggs that they guard until hatching.
ai.distributionRemarks: The King Cobra inhabits the Western Ghats, Northeast India, and the Himalayan foothills, ranging from sea level up to 2,500 meters in dense forests.
